audits.summary: Re-audited the 5 dashboard endpoints against the canonical deployed backend (/tmp/apex-release, release/go-live-2026-06-01). The release tree DOES have dashboard/ (DashboardController + ActivityController + DashboardService) and kpis/ (KpisController + KpiCalculatorService) modules the legacy audit missed — so /activity and /today/kpis are now serviceable (partial, BFF transform needed), NOT gaps. Global prefix is "api" (main.ts:27). OrgScopeGuard is a global APP_GUARD (app.module.ts:58), so EVERY route below is org-scoped automatically from the verified Clerk JWT — the FE never sends an orgId. RESULT: 2 partial (today/kpis, activity), 3 true gaps (notifications, notifications/mark-read, welcome/status) — no Notification model, no User/Org onboarding flags, no notifications/welcome/onboarding controller anywhere in the release source. Key cited files: /tmp/apex-release/apps/api/src/dashboard/dashboard.controller.ts, activity.controller.ts, dashboard.service.ts, /tmp/apex-release/apps/api/src/kpis/kpis.controller.ts, kpi-calculator.service.ts, /tmp/apex-release/packages/db/prisma/schema.prisma (User L174-189, Org L121-154 — no onboarding/notification fields).

NOTE: all dashboard.stats counts are ALL-TIME (no date filter); kpis.quality counts use whereOutreachArtifactsInWindow(orgId, since, status) i.e. updatedAt>=since over a windowDays (default from WindowDto, clamped 1..90).
endpoints.transform: BFF composes TodayKpis from BOTH calls: artifactsPending <- kpis.quality.outreach_artifacts.pending_review; artifactsSentToday <- kpis.quality.outreach_artifacts.sent (call /api/kpis/quality?windowDays=1 to approximate 'today'; otherwise it is window-scoped not calendar-today); qualifiedMeetingsBooked <- dashboard.stats.meetingsBooked; leadsScored <- dashboard.stats.leadsSourced (every LeadScore row = a scored lead) OR sum(A+B+C) from kpis.quality.lead_score_distribution; replyRate7d <- dashboard.stats.replyRate which is constant 0 (no real reply telemetry surfaced here) — BFF passes 0 through; leadsSourcedToday <- NOT directly available calendar-scoped (LeadScore has createdAt but no count-by-day endpoint), BFF must fall back to dashboard.stats.leadsSourced (all-time) or 0.
endpoints.notes: PARTIAL. Org scoping: automatic via global OrgScopeGuard. True gaps within this tile: (1) replyRate7d — backend hardcodes 0 (dashboard.service.ts:60), no 7-day reply-rate computation exists; (2) leadsSourcedToday / artifactsSentToday 'today' calendar semantics — backend offers all-time (dashboard.stats) or rolling windowDays (kpis), neither is calendar-midnight 'today'; windowDays=1 is the closest approximation. No pagination. Read-only, no write/dry-run concerns. A faithful TodayKpis would need a new today-windowed handler + real reply-rate source (EvidenceEvent message.replied is not currently aggregated).

endpoints.real_route: GET /api/activity?limit=N — ActivityController.list() → DashboardService.activity(orgId, limit) (activity.controller.ts:9-20, dashboard.service.ts:65-196)
endpoints.response_shape: Returns { events: ActivityEvent[] } where backend ActivityEvent = { id:string (synthetic e.g. 'run:<id>:started' / 'artifact:<id>:created' / 'meeting:<id>:proposed'), kind: enum('run_started'|'run_needs_approval'|'run_completed'|'run_failed'|'draft_created'|'draft_approved'|'draft_rejected'|'meeting_proposed'|'meeting_confirmed'), text:string (human sentence, e.g. 'Started pipeline-supervisor'), at:string (ISO8601), leadId:string ('' for run/artifact events, personId for meeting events) }. Built by fanning over GraphRun (graphName/status/needsApproval/startedAt/completedAt), OutreachArtifact (toolName/status/createdAt/reviewedAt), MeetingLedger (title/status/personId/createdAt/confirmedAt), merged + sorted desc by `at`, sliced to limit (default 30, clamp 1..100).
endpoints.transform: FE wants a bare ARRAY (not {events:[]}) of FE ActivityEvent = { id, agentName, agentType:enum(sdr|content|ops|pipeline|reply|reporting), action, stage, timestamp, artifactId:string|null, leadId:string|null }. BFF: unwrap resp.events; map each: id <- ev.id; timestamp <- ev.at; action <- ev.text; leadId <- ev.leadId || null; artifactId <- (parse from ev.id when prefix is 'artifact:' -> the middle segment, else null); agentType <- derive from kind ('run_*' -> 'pipeline', 'draft_*' -> 'sdr', 'meeting_*' -> 'pipeline'); agentName <- synthesize from agentType (e.g. 'SDR Agent' / 'Pipeline Supervisor') since backend has no agent identity on the event; stage <- derive from kind (e.g. run_needs_approval -> 'awaiting_approval', draft_created -> 'drafting', meeting_confirmed -> 'meeting'). FE `filter` query param (all|outbound|pipeline|conversations) is NOT supported by backend — BFF applies it client-side over the mapped agentType, or ignores it.
endpoints.notes: PARTIAL. Org scoping automatic (global guard). Field-name mismatch is total (kind/text/at vs agentType/action/timestamp) and several FE fields are SYNTHETIC under BFF mapping: agentName and agentType have no real backend source (no per-event agent attribution) and stage is a derived label — these are best-effort, not ground truth. artifactId must be regex-extracted from the synthetic id string. FE default limit is 50 but backend default is 30 and clamps at 100 — BFF should pass through limit explicitly. The FE `filter` enum has no backend equivalent (must filter in BFF). No pagination cursor; limit-only.

audits.summary:
Re-audited the artifacts domain against the CANONICAL DEPLOYED backend at /tmp/apex-release (release/go-live-2026-06-01). The earlier "legacy" audit was wrong: the OutreachArtifactsController IS real and deployed — OutreachModule is imported in app.module.ts (line 48) and the controller exposes GET/POST artifact routes. ALL routes carry the global prefix `api` (main.ts:27 `app.setGlobalPrefix("api")`) and are org-scoped by the GLOBAL OrgScopeGuard (app.module.ts:58, APP_GUARD) — orgId comes from the verified Clerk JWT via @OrgId() (org-context.decorator.ts), NOT from any query/header/body param. So the BFF must forward the user's auth, NOT pass orgId.

Path-shape mismatch every endpoint must bridge: deployed routes are `/api/outreach-artifacts...` (and `/api/graph/runs/:id/outreach-artifacts`); the FE openapi uses `/artifacts...`. The BFF rewrites the base path.

5 of 7 endpoints are real (list-pending via status filter, list, get, approve, reject) = full/partial. 2 are TRUE GAPS with no deployed route: POST /artifacts/{id}/suppress (SuppressionService exists but is only reachable via the public unsubscribe GET /u/:token flow — there is no authenticated per-artifact suppress endpoint, and no path that flips the artifact to SUPPRESSED on demand) and POST /artifacts/bulk-approve (no controller method, no service method, no loop).

The single biggest response-shape gap across ALL endpoints: the FE OutreachArtifact schema demands rich nested objects — `recipient` (id/name/email/title/company), `citations` (FactCitation[]), `evaluatorScores` (pii/hallucination/citationCoverage/toxicity), `sendPolicy` (4 booleans) — NONE of which exist on the deployed OutreachArtifact prisma model (schema.prisma:647-682). The model has only scalar `recipientRef` (a bare email/id string, no FK to Person), `subject`, `bodyText`, `bodyHtml`, `payload` (Json), `status`, `reviewerNote`, `reviewedBy/At`, `sentAt`, `sendReceiptId`, `graphRunId`, timestamps. Evaluator scores fire INLINE in LangSmith (evaluator-runner.service.ts) and are NOT persisted to any queryable DB table (no EvaluatorFact model in schema.prisma) — so evaluatorScores/citations cannot be hydrated from the DB at read time. The BFF can map scalars 1:1 but must synthesize/stub the 4 nested objects.

endpoints.real_route: GET /api/outreach-artifacts?status=PENDING_REVIEW — OutreachArtifactsController.list() (outreach-artifacts.controller.ts:36-44) → OutreachArtifactsService.listForOrg(orgId, {status: PENDING_REVIEW}) (outreach-artifacts.service.ts:138-147)
endpoints.response_shape: Returns raw OutreachArtifact[] (bare array, NOT an envelope). Each row (prisma model schema.prisma:647-682 / @prisma/client OutreachArtifact): { id:string, orgId:string, graphRunId:string|null, toolName:string, channel:'EMAIL'|'LINKEDIN'|'HUBSPOT_NOTE', recipientRef:string|null, subject:string|null, bodyText:string|null, bodyHtml:string|null, payload:Json, status:'DRAFT'|'PENDING_REVIEW'|'APPROVED'|'REJECTED'|'SENT'|'SUPPRESSED', reviewerNote:string|null, reviewedBy:string|null, reviewedAt:Date|null, sentAt:Date|null, sendReceiptId:string|null, createdAt:Date, updatedAt:Date }. Service hardcodes orderBy createdAt desc and take:100; NO offset/page param.
endpoints.transform: BFF: GET /api/outreach-artifacts?status=PENDING_REVIEW, then map each row via shared artifact-transform (see GET /artifacts/{id}) and wrap into PaginatedArtifacts { items, total, page, limit }. Pagination is BFF-SIDE only: backend always returns up to 100 newest PENDING_REVIEW rows with no count; BFF must slice items by (page,limit) and compute total=items.length from the returned slice (or total=count of returned array). FE default limit=5.
endpoints.notes: Org scoping: handled by global OrgScopeGuard via JWT — BFF forwards user auth, does NOT send orgId. PAGINATION GAP: backend has no page/limit/total — capped at 100 rows, BFF must paginate in-memory and `total` is only accurate up to 100. Read-only, no write-path concern.

endpoints.real_route: GET /api/outreach-artifacts (optional ?status=) — OutreachArtifactsController.list() (controller:36-44) → service.listForOrg() (service:138-147). parseStatus() (controller:81-90) validates against the prisma OutreachArtifactStatus enum (DRAFT|PENDING_REVIEW|APPROVED|REJECTED|SENT|SUPPRESSED).
endpoints.response_shape: Same as above: bare OutreachArtifact[] capped at take:100, orderBy createdAt desc.
endpoints.transform: BFF: pass ?status through (FE enum [PENDING_REVIEW,APPROVED,SENT,REJECTED,SUPPRESSED] is a subset of backend enum — all valid; FE never sends DRAFT). Map rows + wrap in PaginatedArtifacts. BFF-side pagination (page default 1, limit default 20).
endpoints.notes: Backend status enum also includes DRAFT which FE omits — harmless. PAGINATION GAP identical to /pending (100-row cap, no server total). Org-scoped via JWT guard.

endpoints.real_route: GET /api/outreach-artifacts/:id — OutreachArtifactsController.get() (controller:46-50) → service.get(orgId,id) (service:156-162). 404 (NotFoundException) if missing OR if artifact.orgId !== orgId (org isolation enforced in service).
endpoints.response_shape: Single OutreachArtifact (same field set as the list rows above). Notably has NO recipient object, NO citations, NO evaluatorScores, NO sendPolicy — only scalar recipientRef + subject/bodyText/bodyHtml + payload Json.
endpoints.transform: BFF maps the real row → FE OutreachArtifact: id←id; status←status (enum values already match); subject←subject (coalesce null→''); bodyHtml←bodyHtml ?? bodyText (model can have only bodyText); createdAt←createdAt.toISOString(); approvedAt← reviewedAt IF status==='APPROVED' else null; sentAt←sentAt; rejectionReason← reviewerNote IF status==='REJECTED' else null; graphRunId←graphRunId; cohort← (payload.cohort ?? null) best-effort from Json. recipient: SYNTHESIZE { id: recipientRef ?? '', email: recipientRef ?? '', name: payload.name ?? recipientRef ?? '', company: payload.company ?? '', title: payload.title ?? null, avatarUrl: null } — the model has no Person FK so name/company come only from the captured payload Json or are stubbed. citations: [] (NOT stored — gap). evaluatorScores: STUB { pii:0, hallucination:0, citationCoverage:0, toxicity:0 } (NOT persisted in DB — gap). sendPolicy: STUB/derive from org settings (liveSendEnabled/postalAddressSet/unsubscribeConfigured from Org config endpoint; recipientSuppressed would require a SuppressionService.isSuppressed lookup the BFF could add).
endpoints.notes: GAP fields: citations, evaluatorScores have NO backing store (LangSmith-only, no EvaluatorFact prisma model). recipient is best-effort from payload Json (no Person join — recipientRef is a bare string). FE 'required' fields citations/evaluatorScores/sendPolicy must be stubbed to satisfy the schema. Org isolation enforced server-side (orgId mismatch → 404).

endpoints.real_route: POST /api/outreach-artifacts/:id/approve — OutreachArtifactsController.approve() (controller:52-64) → service.approve(orgId,id,reviewedBy) (service:164-205).
endpoints.response_shape: Returns the updated OutreachArtifact (status=APPROVED, reviewedBy set, reviewedAt=now). Side-effect: best-effort enqueue to OutreachSendQueueService for the send worker. 400 BadRequest if status !== PENDING_REVIEW; 404 if not found/wrong org.
endpoints.transform: BFF maps response via the same artifact-transform as GET /{id}. KEY MISMATCH on the request: the deployed route REQUIRES body { reviewedBy } and 400s if absent (controller:59-61), but the FE openapi defines approve with NO requestBody. BFF MUST inject reviewedBy — derive it from the authenticated Clerk user (email or userId from the JWT/ClerkUserId) and send it in the POST body to the backend.
endpoints.notes: Write-path: approve also enqueues a real send (subject to OUTREACH_LIVE_FOR_ORGS gate = tenant-zero only in prod, so non-tenant-zero stays dry-run). BFF must supply reviewedBy from auth context or the call fails with 400. Org-scoped via JWT.

endpoints.real_route: POST /api/outreach-artifacts/:id/reject — OutreachArtifactsController.reject() (controller:66-78) → service.reject(orgId,id,reviewedBy,reviewerNote) (service:207-258).
endpoints.response_shape: Returns updated OutreachArtifact (status=REJECTED, reviewedBy, reviewedAt=now, reviewerNote set). Side-effect: best-effort append generating LangSmith run to apex-bad-sdr-drafts dataset. 400 if status !== PENDING_REVIEW; 404 if not found/wrong org.
endpoints.transform: FE RejectInput is { reason:string }. BFF maps reason → reviewerNote in the backend body, and ALSO must inject reviewedBy (REQUIRED, controller:73-75 400s without it) from the authenticated user. So BFF body = { reviewedBy: <clerk user>, reviewerNote: <reason> }. Response mapped via shared artifact-transform; FE rejectionReason field hydrates from reviewerNote.
endpoints.notes: Full once BFF injects reviewedBy from auth context (FE schema omits it). reason→reviewerNote mapping is clean. Org-scoped via JWT.

endpoints.real_route: NONE. No suppress route on OutreachArtifactsController (controller only has approve/reject). SuppressionService.suppress() exists (suppression.service.ts:44-84) but is ONLY invoked from the PUBLIC unsubscribe flow (unsubscribe.controller.ts GET /u/:token, token-verified, no auth/orgId guard) and from the send worker on bounce/complaint — there is NO authenticated per-artifact suppress endpoint, and nothing flips the artifact to status=SUPPRESSED on demand (SUPPRESSED is only set by the worker pre-send when isSuppressed() hits).
endpoints.response_shape: N/A — no deployed route returns a suppressed artifact. The SUPPRESSED OutreachArtifactStatus enum value exists (schema.prisma:88) but is only produced system-side by send-outreach.worker.ts, not by any reviewer action.
endpoints.transform: No clean transform. To satisfy the FE, the BFF would have to ORCHESTRATE across two non-existent/mismatched primitives: (1) call SuppressionService.suppress (no authenticated REST surface exists — would need a new backend endpoint), and (2) update the artifact status to SUPPRESSED (no service method does this; service.approve/reject only accept PENDING_REVIEW→APPROVED/REJECTED). BFF CANNOT fulfill this read/write contract against the current release without a backend change.
endpoints.notes: TRUE GAP. Requires new backend work: an authenticated POST that both writes an OutreachSuppression row (by recipientRef) AND transitions the artifact to SUPPRESSED. Not shippable from BFF alone. Recommend flagging to backend team or returning 501 from BFF.

endpoints.real_route: NONE. No bulkApprove controller method and no service method. grep across /tmp/apex-release/apps/api/src for bulk-approve/bulkApprove returns zero non-test hits. There is also no DB-backed evaluator-pass signal to drive 'approve artifacts that pass evaluators' (no EvaluatorFact table; scores are LangSmith-only).
endpoints.response_shape: N/A. FE expects BulkApproveResult { approved:int, skipped:int, reasons:string[] }. Nothing in the release produces this.
endpoints.transform: BFF COULD fake a partial bulk-approve by fanning out N single POST /api/outreach-artifacts/:id/approve calls (loop over PENDING_REVIEW ids), counting successes as `approved` and 400s/404s as `skipped` with `reasons` = collected error messages. BUT the spec's intent ('approve artifacts that PASS EVALUATORS') cannot be honored: there is no queryable per-artifact evaluator score in the DB to gate on, so the BFF would approve indiscriminately (no eval gate).
endpoints.notes: TRUE GAP for the evaluator-gated semantics. A naive BFF fan-out of single-approve calls is possible but loses the 'pass evaluators' guarantee and is N round-trips (each also injecting reviewedBy from auth, and each enqueues a real send under the OUTREACH_LIVE gate). Recommend a real backend bulk endpoint that joins evaluator scores, or down-scope the FE feature.

audits.summary: Re-audited the leads domain against the canonical deployed backend at /tmp/apex-release. Global prefix is `api` (main.ts:27), and both LeadsController (@Controller("leads")) and PipelineController (@Controller("pipeline")) are mounted. Verdict by endpoint: GET /leads is PARTIAL — a real route exists (GET /api/leads → LeadsService.listLeadsForUi) returning a genuine person-derived lead list, but its shape and query params diverge substantially from the openapi Lead/PaginatedLeads contract (different field names, no cohort/intentSignals/sendPolicy/emailStatus enum, envelope is {leads,total} not {items,total,page,limit}, query params are min_score/per_page/search not minScore/limit/q, and stage/geo/cohort/industry/intentSignal filters are mostly unsupported server-side). GET /leads/{id} is a GAP for the literal id but PARTIAL via the analogous GET /api/leads/people/:id (getPersonDetail) — there is no `/leads/{id}` route and no researchBrief/scoreBreakdown(fit/intent/engagement/timing)/recentEvidenceEvents assembled anywhere; the BFF would have to compose it. POST /leads/{id}/trigger-outbound is a GAP — no per-lead outbound trigger exists; the only orchestration entry is POST /api/pipeline/run (org-wide, all-ICP graph run) which is not per-lead and returns a different shape. POST /leads/bulk-suppress is a GAP at the HTTP layer — OutreachSuppression model + SuppressionService.suppress() exist and work, but they key on recipientRef (lowercased email), there is NO public JSON route (only the signed-token unsubscribe GET in unsubscribe.controller.ts), and the FE sends person ids not emails, so the BFF must resolve ids→emails and there is no batch endpoint to call. Earlier audit was right that these write/detail routes are missing; only the list route materially exists.

endpoints.real_route: GET /api/leads → LeadsController.listLeads (leads.controller.ts:46-65) → LeadsService.listLeadsForUi (leads.service.ts:1072-1232)
endpoints.response_shape: { leads: Array<{ id:string; name:string (firstName+lastName); title:string; company:string; domain:string; email:string; industry:string; companySize:string (Company.employeeRange); techStack:string[]; score:number (LeadScore.score); scoreBreakdown:Array<{label:string;value:number}>; stage:'sourced'|'enriched'|'qualified'|'in_crm'|'contacted'|'replied'|'meeting' (DERIVED from meeting/contacted/qualifiedAt/email, never persisted); source:'discovery' (hardcoded); emailStatus:'not_sent'|'sent'|'opened'|'replied'|'bounced' (only not_sent/sent ever emitted — derived from stage); timeline:[] (always empty); createdAt:string ISO }>; total:number }. Source = prisma.person + company + scores + emails(top by confidence) + outreachArtifact + meetingLedger. Accepted query params: stage, min_score, page, per_page(max100,default50), search.
endpoints.transform: Rename envelope {leads,total} → {items: leads.map(...), total, page, limit}. Per lead: id,name,title,email,company,createdAt pass through; domain/industry pass through (nullable ok); companySize → headcountEstimate; score→score (cast int). MISSING fields the BFF must synthesize/default: companyLogoUrl/avatarUrl→null; geo/country→derive from nothing available here (null/empty); cohort:'A'|'B'→synthesize (e.g. score-threshold) — NOT in backend; emailStatus enum mismatch (backend uses lowercase not_sent/sent; openapi expects DELIVERABLE/HIGH_PROBABILITY/CATCH_ALL — must map from EmailCandidate.verified/confidence, which listLeadsForUi does NOT return, so BFF either calls a second query or defaults HIGH_PROBABILITY); intentSignals:[]→backend has none, default []; sendPolicy→synthesize from SendPolicy schema (not provided here); lastContactedAt→null (timeline empty, sentAt not surfaced). scoreBreakdown shape differs ({label,value} vs LeadDetail's {fit,intent,engagement,timing}) — only relevant for detail. Map FE query q→search, limit→per_page, minScore→min_score; page passes through. NOTE: filters geo/cohort/industry/intentSignal/sort are NOT honored server-side — BFF must filter/sort in-memory after fetch (and page math breaks because total comes pre-filter; backend already does this for `stage` at service.ts:1230 returning post-filtered leads but pre-filter total).
endpoints.notes: Org-scoped via @OrgId() decorator (X-Org-Id / org-context) → where company.orgId. Pagination is page/per_page (1-based, max per_page 100). total is the PRE-stage-filter count (service.ts:1134 counts before the in-memory stage filter at 1230) so total can exceed items length when stage filter applied — pagination is subtly buggy for filtered views. No write path. Real gap from contract: cohort, intentSignals, sendPolicy, proper emailStatus enum, geo/country, logo/avatar — all absent in backend, BFF must default or synthesize.

endpoints.real_route: NO /api/leads/{id} route exists. Closest deployed: GET /api/leads/people/:id → LeadsController.getPersonDetail (leads.controller.ts:207-214) → LeadsService.getPersonDetail (leads.service.ts:979-1016)
endpoints.response_shape: getPersonDetail returns: { id:string; firstName:string; lastName:string; title:string|null; company:string|null; companyDomain:string|null; seniority:Seniority; department:Department; linkedinUrl:string|null; location:null (hardcoded); bio:null (hardcoded); bestEmail:string|null; score:number|null (LeadScore.score); qualifiedAt:Date|null; emails:Array<{email;pattern;source;confidence;verified;verificationResult}>; scoreBreakdown:Array<{category:string;points:number}> (only a single {category:'Total',points:score} row) }. EvidenceEvent model exists (schema.prisma:156-172: id,orgId,runId,traceId,kind,refType,refId,payload,createdAt) but getPersonDetail does NOT query it.
endpoints.transform: Path mismatch: FE GET /leads/{id} must be proxied by BFF to GET /api/leads/people/{id}. Build LeadDetail.lead from getPersonDetail (name=firstName+lastName, title, company, domain=companyDomain, email=bestEmail, score, createdAt missing here so default; same synthesized cohort/intentSignals/sendPolicy/emailStatus gaps as list). LeadDetail.researchBrief → NO source (no brief field returned) → default '' or BFF must separately query OutreachArtifact/EvidenceEvent payloads. LeadDetail.scoreBreakdown needs {fit,intent,engagement,timing} ints — backend only returns {category:'Total',points} so BFF must map the single total into one bucket and zero the rest (lossy) OR parse LeadScore.breakdown JSON directly (not exposed by this method). LeadDetail.recentEvidenceEvents → BFF must do its own prisma.evidenceEvent.findMany({where:{orgId, refId: personId}, orderBy createdAt desc}) since getPersonDetail doesn't include them; map {id, kind→eventType, payload→description, createdAt→timestamp}.

Three of the four LeadDetail fields (researchBrief, fit/intent/engagement/timing breakdown, recentEvidenceEvents) are NOT assembled by any deployed method — BFF must compose them from separate queries (evidence_event table is queryable; researchBrief has no real source on release/go-live-2026-06-01 and is effectively a gap).

endpoints.real_route: NONE per-lead. No route matches /leads/:id/trigger-outbound (confirmed: only @Post in leads.controller.ts are icp, icp/:id/schedule, discover). Nearest orchestration: POST /api/pipeline/run → PipelineController.run (pipeline.controller.ts:58-107) → GraphService.runPipelineGraph (graph.service.ts:50-102), which is ORG-WIDE / all-ICP, not lead-scoped.

It enqueues a whole LangGraph supervisor run across every ICP profile in the org (single-flight: 409 ConflictException if a graph is already RUNNING/AWAITING_APPROVAL). It does NOT accept or target a single lead/person id.

BFF could map graphRunId→runId, queued=(graphRunId!=null), message→message, but this triggers the ENTIRE org pipeline, ignoring the {id} path param — semantically wrong and dangerous (single-flight lock means second call 409s). There is no plumbing to start outbound for one specific lead. Honest answer: surface this as not-implemented (501/feature flag) rather than aliasing to pipeline/run.
endpoints.notes: True gap. The graph supervisor is the single entry point (legacy per-target triggerDiscovery is deprecated, leads.controller.ts:138). Per-lead outbound would require a new backend route that seeds a graph run / outreach artifact for one personId — does not exist on release. Org scoping present on pipeline/run but lead targeting absent. Single-flight conflict (graph.service.ts:60-70) makes any per-lead aliasing unreliable.

endpoints.real_route: NO public JSON route. OutreachSuppression model (schema.prisma:812-828) + SuppressionService.suppress() (outreach/suppression.service.ts:44-83) exist, but suppress() is an internal injectable only invoked by the signed-token GET unsubscribe flow (outreach/unsubscribe.controller.ts:44). There is no @Post controller accepting a list of ids/emails to suppress, and no batch method.
endpoints.response_shape: SuppressionService.suppress({orgId, recipientRef, reason, source, metadata?}) returns {created:boolean} per single recipient. recipientRef is a lowercased/trimmed EMAIL (schema comment lines 802-804), unique on (orgId, recipientRef), idempotent (re-suppress returns created:false). No count/affected aggregate is returned and no batch variant exists.
endpoints.transform: openapi expects POST body BulkLeadIds={ids:string[]} (lead/person ids) → BulkActionResult={affected:int}. Backend keys suppression on EMAIL not person id, and exposes no HTTP endpoint. To satisfy the contract the BFF would have to: (1) for each id, resolve person→bestEmail (e.g. via a Person/EmailCandidate query — getPersonDetail gives bestEmail one at a time), (2) call SuppressionService.suppress per email with reason=MANUAL, source='bulk-suppress-ui' — but SuppressionService is NOT reachable over HTTP, so the BFF cannot invoke it without a new backend route, (3) count created===true results → affected. None of (1)-(3) is wired on release/go-live-2026-06-01.
endpoints.notes: True gap at the API boundary: model + service logic exist and are production-grade, but no public mutation endpoint and an id↔email impedance mismatch. Closing it needs a new org-scoped @Post('leads/bulk-suppress') that resolves ids→emails and loops SuppressionService.suppress (dry-run-friendly: it's idempotent and writes only the suppression table, no external send). Until then the BFF cannot honestly return an accurate `affected` count.

audits.summary: HONEST verdict against the DEPLOYED release/go-live-2026-06-01 backend: the conversations domain is almost entirely a GAP. There is NO conversation/inbox/message/thread store. No `/conversations` controller exists anywhere in /tmp/apex-release/apps/api/src. The Prisma schema (/tmp/apex-release/packages/db/prisma/schema.prisma) has NO Conversation, Message, Thread, Inbox, or ReplyIntelligence model — the only `threadId` columns (GraphRun line 584, GraphCheckpoint line 608) are LangGraph checkpoint thread ids, NOT email conversation threads. The closest deployed surfaces are: (1) a BetaStubsController `GET /api/inbox` that returns a hardcoded `[]` (beta-stubs.controller.ts:19-22); (2) Gmail proxy endpoints `GET /api/integrations/gmail/messages` and `GET /api/integrations/gmail/threads/:threadId` (gmail.controller.ts:137-172) that proxy Google's API live and return raw Gmail message shapes — but only when a Gmail Integration row is CONNECTED, and they carry NO sentiment/reply-intelligence/unread/needsReply/archived state; (3) the OutreachArtifact table (schema line 647) which is OUTBOUND-only (subject/bodyText/bodyHtml/status) with no inbound side, no thread grouping, no conversation-state fields. Inbound Gmail replies are NOT persisted: gmail.service.ts maybeDispatchReply() (line 242) just triggers a Reply Handler agent run and writes the inbound context to AgentLog (line 290). The reply-handler produces an ephemeral `{type:'reply_draft', intent, draft}` JSON in-run (runtime/prompts/reply-handler.ts) that is never stored as a draft entity. None of the FE conversation-state fields (archived, unread, needsReply, lastMessageAt, lastMessagePreview, replyIntelligence, sentiment, nextBestAction) exist in any controller, service, or model. ALL FOUR endpoints are GAP. A real implementation requires NEW Prisma models (Conversation + ConversationMessage + ReplyIntelligence), an ingestion path to persist inbound/outbound emails into them, a sentiment/NBA classifier to populate replyIntelligence, and a new conversations module. The earlier audit's "missed controllers" correction does NOT apply here — unlike dashboard/kpis/meetings/pipeline/runs, there genuinely is no conversations controller in the release tree.

endpoints.real_route: NONE — closest is GET /api/inbox (beta-stubs.controller.ts:19-22) which returns hardcoded []; and GET /api/integrations/gmail/messages (gmail.controller.ts:137 -> gmail.service.ts:437 listMessages) which proxies Gmail live. No org-scoped conversation thread store exists. No Conversation Prisma model exists in schema.prisma.
endpoints.response_shape: GET /api/inbox returns `[]` (unknown[]). GET /api/integrations/gmail/messages returns `{ messages: GmailMessage[], nextPageToken?: string }` where GmailMessage = { id:string, threadId:string, snippet:string, from:string, to:string, subject:string, date:string, labelIds:string[], body?:string } (gmail.service.ts:60-69). NO leadName/leadCompany/unread/needsReply/archived/replyIntelligence/sentiment fields anywhere.
endpoints.transform: No viable transform to PaginatedConversations { items:Conversation[], total, page, limit }. The beta-stub yields an empty list (BFF could pass through {items:[],total:0,page,limit} for a clean empty state). Gmail messages cannot be mapped: they lack lead linkage, thread-level subject/lastMessage rollup, unread/needsReply/archived flags, and the entire replyIntelligence{sentiment,sentimentConfidence,nextBestAction,nextBestActionType} block, none of which exist in the backend. Required: NEW Conversation model + ingestion + sentiment/NBA classifier.
endpoints.notes: TRUE GAP. Query params sentiment/unread/needsReply/archived/leadId/page/limit have no backing data. Org scoping: OrgScopeGuard is global so an org-scoped query would work IF a model existed. Recommend BFF returns empty PaginatedConversations until a Conversation model + Gmail-thread ingestion pipeline is built.

endpoints.real_route: NONE — closest is GET /api/integrations/gmail/threads/:threadId (gmail.controller.ts:169 -> gmail.service.ts getThread) which proxies a Gmail thread live, requires a CONNECTED Gmail integration, and uses the Gmail thread id (not an internal conversation id).
endpoints.response_shape: getThread returns GmailThread = { id, messages: GmailMessage[], ... } where each GmailMessage = { id, threadId, snippet, from, to, subject, date, labelIds[], body }. NO direction(inbound/outbound) field (must be inferred from labelIds SENT/INBOX), NO senderName parse, NO bodyHtml split (body is text or html opportunistically), and NO conversation-level subject/unread/needsReply/archived or replyIntelligence. No pendingDraftId — reply drafts are never persisted (reply-handler output is ephemeral; only logged to AgentLog).
endpoints.transform: No faithful transform to ConversationDetail { conversation:Conversation, messages:ConversationMessage[], pendingDraftId }. A partial mapping of Gmail thread messages -> ConversationMessage is conceivable (id; direction from labelIds.includes('SENT')?'outbound':'inbound'; bodyHtml<=body; sentAt<=date; senderName<=parse(from)), but the wrapping Conversation object (leadName/leadCompany/unread/needsReply/archived/replyIntelligence) has NO source data, and pendingDraftId has no store. Requires NEW Conversation+ConversationMessage+ReplyIntelligence models.
endpoints.notes: TRUE GAP. Even the Gmail proxy only works for orgs with a live Gmail OAuth integration and keys off Gmail's threadId, not an internal conversation id; tenant-zero is the only org with live Gmail. replyIntelligence (sentiment + nextBestAction) is unbuildable without a new classifier service.

endpoints.real_route: NONE. The reply-drafting capability exists ONLY as an in-run LLM step in the Reply Handler agent (runtime/prompts/reply-handler.ts producing {type:'reply_draft',intent,draft}), triggered automatically by Gmail push (gmail.service.ts:242 maybeDispatchReply -> runtime.triggerRun). There is no HTTP route to draft a reply for a given conversation, and the draft is never persisted as an entity.
endpoints.response_shape: N/A — no endpoint. The async path: RuntimeService.triggerRun(agentId, orgId) returns an AgentRun (id, status...). The reply_draft itself is ephemeral LLM JSON consumed within the executor; the only persistence is an AgentLog row with the inbound context metadata (gmail.service.ts:285-292). FE expects TriggerResult { runId:string, queued:boolean, message:string }.
endpoints.transform: Partial-shape mapping is possible ONLY if a new controller wired draft-reply to runtime.triggerRun on the org's Reply Handler agent: map run.id -> runId, queued:true, message:'Reply draft queued'. But this cannot target a specific conversation id (no conversation store), cannot return the drafted text, and would trigger a full agent run rather than a scoped single-reply draft. Real fix: persist a ReplyDraft entity and expose a synchronous/async draft endpoint keyed by conversation id.
endpoints.notes: TRUE GAP for the contract as written. The underlying LLM reply-drafting logic IS deployed and sophisticated (fail-closed, intent classification), but there is no addressable conversation, no draft persistence, and no HTTP entry point. TriggerResult shape is trivially satisfiable but semantically wrong without a conversation store.

endpoints.real_route: NONE. No archive route exists. No `archived` field exists on any Prisma model (grep over schema.prisma + all controllers/services found zero `archived` conversation-state references; only an unrelated comment in unsubscribe-token.util.ts). Gmail proxy has no archive/modify-labels endpoint exposed.
endpoints.response_shape: N/A — no endpoint and no archivable entity. FE expects BulkActionResult { affected:integer }.
endpoints.transform: No transform possible — there is nothing to archive. A BFF could return { affected:0 } or { affected:1 } as a no-op stub to keep the UI from erroring, but no state would actually change. Real fix: add `archived Boolean` to a new Conversation model and a PATCH/POST archive handler (could also call Gmail users.messages.modify to remove INBOX label, but that endpoint is not currently exposed by the deployed gmail.controller).
endpoints.notes: TRUE GAP. Org-scoping would be fine via the global OrgScopeGuard once a model exists. Until then this is a pure stub at best.

audits.summary:
Re-audited against the deployed release tree (/tmp/apex-release). Global prefix is `app.setGlobalPrefix("api")` (main.ts:27), and every route is org-scoped via OrgScopeGuard → `@OrgId()` (common/org-context.decorator.ts), so the BFF never trusts client-supplied orgId.

CRITICAL CORRECTION vs the openapi intent: there are TWO distinct "run" concepts in the release. (1) RunsController @Controller("runs") operates on the legacy `AgentRun` executor model (runs.controller.ts + runs.service.ts). (2) GraphController @Controller("graph") operates on the `GraphRun` LangGraph-supervisor model (graph.controller.ts + graph.service.ts). The openapi spec for /runs explicitly says "Paginated GraphRun history", "GraphRunDetail", "evidence timeline", and the PaginatedRuns/GraphRun schema enum {RUNNING, AWAITING_APPROVAL, COMPLETED, FAILED} matches GraphRunStatus — NOT RunStatus. So the BFF MUST back /runs and /runs/{id} with the `graph/runs` routes, and back /runs/trigger with `POST /api/pipeline/run` (which calls GraphService.runPipelineGraph). The legacy /api/runs* routes are the wrong source for this FE contract.

GET /agents is FULL: GET /api/agents (AgentsController.findAll → AgentsService.findAll) returns the agent roster; needs a straightforward field/enum transform.

GET /runs and POST /runs/trigger are PARTIAL: the GraphRun row lacks several openapi fields (agentsInvolved, leadsSourced, artifactsGenerated, durationMs, costUsd, triggeredBy) — most are derivable in the BFF from the `state` JSON snapshot (counts.*), graphName, and startedAt/completedAt, but costUsd has no per-run column (only aggregated from EvidenceEvent.payload.cost_usd in kpi-calculator) and triggeredBy is not persisted on GraphRun.

GET /runs/{id} (GraphRunDetail = run + evidence timeline) is PARTIAL→GAP on the timeline: GET /api/graph/runs/:id returns the GraphRun row (incl. `state` snapshot) for the `run` half, but there is NO deployed endpoint that serves a per-run evidence timeline of TimelineNode objects. EvidenceEvent rows exist (evidence_event table, written by EvidenceLedgerService, indexed by runId) but no controller reads them out — so the `timeline` array must come from EvidenceEvent directly in the BFF (raw prisma/SQL) or be returned empty.

endpoints.real_route: GET /api/graph/runs — GraphController.list (graph.controller.ts:16) → GraphService.listGraphRuns(orgId, limit=20) (graph.service.ts:182). NOTE: the legacy GET /api/runs (RunsController.findByOrg → RunsService.findByOrg, runs.service.ts:9) returns AgentRun rows with RunStatus enum {QUEUED,RUNNING,COMPLETED,FAILED,CANCELLED,PENDING_APPROVAL} — wrong shape/enum for this FE contract, do NOT use it.
endpoints.response_shape: GraphService.listGraphRuns returns GraphRun[] (NOT an envelope, NOT paginated). Each GraphRun (schema.prisma:580): { id:string; orgId:string; threadId:string; graphName:string (e.g. 'pipeline-supervisor'); status: GraphRunStatus 'RUNNING'|'AWAITING_APPROVAL'|'COMPLETED'|'FAILED'|'CANCELLED'; currentNode:string|null; state: Json|null (snapshotPublicState shape: { orgId, icpProfileIds, stagesCompleted, counts:{companies,people,scored,outreach}, approved, approvedBy, messages[], errors[] }); needsApproval:boolean; approvedAt:DateTime|null; approvedBy:string|null; error:string|null; startedAt:DateTime; completedAt:DateTime|null; langsmithRootRunId:string|null }. Ordered startedAt desc, hard-capped at 20.
endpoints.transform: Map GraphRun[] → PaginatedRuns { items, total, page, limit }. Per item → GraphRun openapi schema: id←id; status←status (drop CANCELLED to FAILED, or pass through — openapi enum omits CANCELLED, so map CANCELLED→FAILED); startedAt←startedAt.toISOString(); completedAt←completedAt?.toISOString()||null; leadsSourced←state.counts.scored ?? state.counts.companies ?? 0; artifactsGenerated←state.counts.outreach ?? 0; durationMs←completedAt? (completedAt-startedAt) :(now-startedAt); agentsInvolved←derive from graphName/state.stagesCompleted (e.g. ['supervisor','sourcing','enrichment','scoring','outreach']); triggeredBy←approvedBy ?? 'system'; costUsd←0 (NOT on row). Envelope: total=items.length (no total from backend), page=1, limit=20. GAP: backend ignores page/limit/status query params — BFF can post-filter status client-side but cannot truly paginate (listGraphRuns hard-caps 20).
endpoints.notes: Org-scoped (orgId required, BadRequestException if absent). Response is a bare array, not {runs:[]} nor {items,total,...} — this is the same envelope mismatch class as the prior Approve-button bug (MEMORY graph-runs-envelope-mismatch). True gaps: no server-side pagination (limit fixed 20, no offset/page, no total count), no status query filter, costUsd not persisted per-run, triggeredBy not persisted (only approvedBy). If FE needs real pagination/total, that's a backend change.

endpoints.real_route: POST /api/pipeline/run — PipelineController.run (pipeline.controller.ts:58, @HttpCode(202)) → GraphService.runPipelineGraph(orgId, icpProfileIds) (graph.service.ts:50). This is the GraphRun-producing trigger that matches the FE intent ('Start a new pipeline run'). NOTE: legacy POST /api/runs (RunsController.create) creates an AgentRun for a specific agentId and requires a CreateRunDto body {agentId} — different concept; the proper agent-scoped trigger is POST /api/agents/:id/runs (AgentsController.triggerRun → RuntimeService.triggerRun).
endpoints.response_shape: PipelineController.run returns { message:string; autoGenerated:{id,name}|null; graphRunId:string|null; triggered:Array<{icpProfileId,name}>; skipped:Array<{icpProfileId,name,reason}>; stage:string }. It auto-generates an ICP if the org has none, then enqueues the LangGraph supervisor (returns immediately; graph runs in background). 202 Accepted. runPipelineGraph throws ConflictException if a graph is already RUNNING/AWAITING_APPROVAL for the org (single-flight).
endpoints.transform: Map → TriggerResult { runId, queued, message }: runId←graphRunId (null if start failed); queued←(graphRunId!=null); message←message (pass through). On 409 ConflictException (graph already in-flight) the BFF should surface queued=false with the conflict message, or translate to a 409. openapi declares 202 — preserve it.
endpoints.notes: Org-scoped. openapi /runs/trigger has NO request body; pipeline/run accepts optional {stage} which BFF can omit (defaults to 'full'). Side-effecting WRITE path → enqueues a real LangGraph supervisor run; recommend the BFF gate this behind the same dry-run/allowlist posture as outreach (OUTREACH_LIVE_FOR_ORGS=tenant-zero per MEMORY golive-deploy). The single-flight conflict is real behavior the FE must handle.

endpoints.real_route: GET /api/graph/runs/:id — GraphController.get (graph.controller.ts:22) → GraphService.getGraphRun(orgId, runId) (graph.service.ts:174) covers the `run` half ONLY. There is NO deployed route serving a per-run evidence TimelineNode[] — the openapi-listed /graph-runs/{id}/timeline (tag: activity) has no backend implementation. ActivityController @Controller('activity') (activity.controller.ts) only has GET /api/activity (org-wide feed), not /:id/timeline, and it builds coarse ActivityEvent rows from GraphRun+OutreachArtifact+MeetingLedger, NOT TimelineNode.
endpoints.response_shape: getGraphRun returns a single GraphRun row (same fields as listGraphRuns item above; 404 NotFoundException if not in org). The real per-step evidence data lives in the EvidenceEvent table (schema.prisma:156, @@map('evidence_event')): { id; orgId; runId:string|null; traceId:string|null; kind:string (leadSourced|leadScored|messageDrafted|qaPass|qaFail|approvalRequested|approvalGranted|approvalDenied|artifactPersisted|messageSent|crmSynced...); refType:string; refId:string; payload:Json (may include cost_usd, duration_ms); createdAt:DateTime }. Written by EvidenceLedgerService (observability/evidence-ledger.service.ts), indexed @@index([runId]) — but exposed by NO controller.
endpoints.transform: BFF builds GraphRunDetail: run←transform getGraphRun output to the openapi GraphRun schema (same mapping as GET /runs item). timeline←REQUIRES the BFF to query EvidenceEvent directly (raw prisma against evidence_event WHERE runId=:id AND orgId=:org ORDER BY createdAt ASC), then map each EvidenceEvent → TimelineNode { id←id; nodeType←map kind→{agent_run|llm_call|evaluator|tool_call|human_action} (approval* → human_action; qaPass/qaFail → evaluator; messageDrafted → llm_call; messageSent/crmSynced → tool_call; else agent_run); label←kind; summary←derive from payload; reasoning←payload.reasoning||null; tokensUsed←payload.tokens||null; durationMs←payload.duration_ms||null; cost←payload.cost_usd||null; score←payload.score||null; timestamp←createdAt.toISOString(); children←[] (flat, no nesting persisted) }. If BFF cannot reach evidence_event, return timeline:[] (run still renders).
endpoints.notes: TRUE GAP for the timeline half: no deployed HTTP endpoint returns TimelineNode[]; the data exists in evidence_event but is read-only-internal (EvidenceLedger writes, kpi-calculator + run-level-evaluator read). Options: (a) BFF reads evidence_event directly via its own prisma/DB connection (org-scope on orgId — feasible since the table is org-keyed), or (b) backend adds a GET /api/graph/runs/:id/timeline route (recommended fast-follow). The `run` half is FULL via GET /api/graph/runs/:id. Org-scoped + 404 honored.

endpoints.real_route: GET /api/agents — AgentsController.findAll (agents.controller.ts:61) → AgentsService.findAll(orgId) (agents.service.ts:25).
endpoints.response_shape: Returns Agent[] (bare array). Each row (schema.prisma:208) includes template + _count.runs: { id:string; orgId:string; templateId:string; name:string; domain: Domain enum (SALES|MARKETING|OPS); config:Json; schedule:string|null (cron); status: AgentStatus 'ACTIVE'|'PAUSED'|'ERROR'|'DEPLOYING'; createdAt:DateTime; updatedAt:DateTime; template: AgentTemplate{id,domain,name,description,systemPrompt,defaultConfig,requiredIntegrations[],isActive,...}; _count:{ runs:number } }. Ordered createdAt desc.
endpoints.transform: Map Agent[] → openapi Agent[]: id←id; name←name; type←map domain/template.name → enum {sdr,content,ops,pipeline,reply,reporting} (SALES→'sdr', MARKETING→'content', OPS→'ops'; refine via template.name when available); status←map AgentStatus → {idle,running,error} (ACTIVE→'idle' unless a run is in flight, PAUSED→'idle', ERROR→'error', DEPLOYING→'running'); lastAction←null (or derive from most-recent AgentRun — not in findAll payload, would need GET /api/agents/:id which includes runs[]); lastActionAt←null similarly; recentActivityCount←_count.runs; sparklineData←[] or derive from per-agent run counts (getAnalytics has runsByDay if needed). All required openapi fields (id,name,type,status,recentActivityCount,sparklineData) are satisfiable.
endpoints.notes: Org-scoped via @OrgId(). FULL. Caveat: lastAction/lastActionAt and a real sparkline aren't in the findAll payload — findAll only includes _count.runs, not run rows. For populated lastAction/sparkline the BFF would N+1 to GET /api/agents/:id/analytics (AgentsService.getAnalytics returns runsByDay[7] + recentRuns[5]) or accept nulls (both fields are nullable/non-required in openapi). Status→{idle,running,error} mapping loses PAUSED/DEPLOYING granularity by design.

audits.summary:
Re-audited the settings domain against the CANONICAL deployed backend at /tmp/apex-release (release/go-live-2026-06-01), READ-ONLY. Global prefix is `/api` (main.ts:27 `app.setGlobalPrefix("api")`); OrgScopeGuard is global and derives orgId from the verified Clerk `org_id` claim (common/org-scope.guard.ts) — every route below is auto org-scoped, FE never passes orgId. There is NO `settings` controller; the FE `/settings/*` contract must be composed by the BFF from orgs/, integrations/, billing/, and leads/ controllers.

Reality vs the openapi.yaml contract: roughly 4/18 endpoints are FULL or near-full, ~5 PARTIAL (real data exists but shape/field gaps), and ~9 are TRUE GAPS with no backend at all. The big confirmed gaps the earlier (legacy-tree) audit also would have hit, and which DO NOT exist in the release tree either: cadence, style, team list/invite/remove, api-keys CRUD, and notification-prefs. There is no Cadence/Style/ApiKey/NotificationPref model in schema.prisma and no controller route for any of them.

Important correction to the FE assumption that PUT /settings/org can update sender identity / compliance: the real update path is `PATCH /api/orgs/:id` but its DTO (common/dto/orgs.dto.ts UpdateOrgDto) only accepts name/plan/website. The Org model HAS the columns senderName, country, physicalAddress — but OrgsService.update() (orgs.service.ts:124) ignores them, so PUT /settings/org is only partially wired even though the columns exist. liveSendEnabled / timezone / logoUrl / unsubscribeUrl / creditsRemaining / welcomeComplete have NO backing column on Org at all.

ICP is real but lives under leads/, not settings: GET/POST /api/leads/icp (leads.controller.ts:69,108). It returns IcpProfile[] with DIFFERENT field names (targetTitles/targetIndustries/targetGeos/intentKeywords/techStackSignals/minEmployees/maxEmployees) than the FE IcpProfile (titles/industries/geos/intentSignals/sizeBand + an exclusionDomains the backend lacks). No PUT — only create-new + a schedule POST. BFF can map GET (take most-recent profile) and route PUT→POST(create).

Integrations is the strongest match: GET /api/integrations + POST /api/integrations/:provider/connect + POST /api/integrations/:provider/disconnect map almost 1:1, but the backend Integration row exposes status as the IntegrationStatus enum (PENDING/CONNECTED/ERROR/REVOKED, uppercase) vs FE connected/available/errored, has no accountEmail/errorMessage at top level (errorMessage is `lastErrorMessage`), and credentials are encrypted (never expose). suppressionCount has no count endpoint — SuppressionService (outreach/suppression.service.ts) only has isSuppressed/suppress; BFF must Prisma-count OutreachSuppression directly or return 0.

All file citations are absolute paths under /tmp/apex-release/apps/api/src and /tmp/apex-release/packages/db/prisma/schema.prisma.

endpoints.real_route: GET /api/orgs/me — OrgsController.findMe (/tmp/apex-release/apps/api/src/orgs/orgs.controller.ts:57); service OrgsService.findByClerkUser (/tmp/apex-release/apps/api/src/orgs/orgs.service.ts:115). auth.model:
org-scope.guard.ts is registered as the FIRST global APP_GUARD (apex-release/apps/api/src/app.module.ts:58, `{ provide: APP_GUARD, useClass: OrgScopeGuard }`), so it runs on every route except those marked `@SkipOrgGuard()`.

HOW IT AUTHORIZES (canActivate, org-scope.guard.ts:58-139):
1. It does NOT require a Clerk `org_id` claim. The guard considers Clerk "configured" if CLERK_DOMAIN or CLERK_JWKS_URL is set (lines 42-45). In prod it requires `Authorization: Bearer <JWT>` (lines 73-76) and verifies the signature via verifyClerkToken (jwt.util.ts: fetches Clerk JWKS, checks exp, verifies RS256). It extracts `clerkUserId = payload.sub` and `clerkOrgRole = payload.org_role` (lines 87-88).
2. org_id resolution branch (lines 90-112): `if (payload.org_id) { orgId = payload.org_id }` ELSE — and on THIS instance Clerk Organizations is DISABLED so `payload.org_id` is always undefined — it falls to the DB resolution path: `prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { clerkId: clerkUserId }, select: { orgId: true } })` and sets `orgId = user.orgId`. If no User row exists yet, it calls `autoProvisionOrg(payload)` (lines 164-221) which creates an Org+OWNER User keyed on the signature-verified `sub` and returns its id. So org is derived SOLELY from the verified `sub` claim → User.clerkId → User.orgId.
3. Final resolve (resolveOrg, lines 145-155): treats the resolved id as our internal cuid first (Org.findUnique by id), falling back to Org.slug. On the DB-resolution path the value is already our internal Org.id so the by-id lookup hits. Then it sets `request.orgId = org.id`, `request.clerkUserId`, `request.clerkOrgRole` (lines 135-137); these are read by the @OrgId()/@ClerkUserId() param decorators (org-context.decorator.ts). 403 "Organization not found" if the org row is missing; 401 if no/invalid token.

Note: the guard ALSO has a non-prod-only `x-org-id` header fallback gated on `NODE_ENV !== 'production' && ALLOW_DEV_ORG_HEADER === 'true'` (lines 46-48, 113-122) — never active in prod. In prod, the only path is JWT `sub` → DB. So: NO org_id claim is needed or used on this instance; org is resolved from the Clerk user (sub) via the User table.
auth.org_resolution:
The deployed backend maps Clerk user → org by `User.clerkId == payload.sub`, then reads `User.orgId`. Prisma model (apex-release/packages/db/prisma/schema.prisma:174-189): User has `orgId String`, `org Org @relation`, `clerkId String? @unique`, `role UserRole @default(MEMBER)`; `@@index([clerkId])`. Org (lines 121-154): `id String @id @default(cuid())`, `slug String @unique`.

Two relevant org endpoints (apex-release/apps/api/src/orgs/orgs.controller.ts), BOTH `@SkipOrgGuard()` because the JWT may have no org context yet (chicken-and-egg). They verify the bearer token inline via the controller-local `verifyAuth(req)` (orgs.controller.ts:147-161), which calls verifyClerkToken and returns `{ clerkUserId: payload.sub, email: payload.email ?? '' }`:

1) `GET /api/orgs/me` (controller line 57-62) → `orgsService.findByClerkUser(clerkUserId)` (orgs.service.ts:115-122): `prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { clerkId }, include: { org: { include: { agents: true, integrations: true } } } })` and returns `user.org` (or `null` if no user). This is the canonical "who am I / what's my org" call; response = the full Org row (id, name, slug, website, physicalAddress, country, senderName, plan, trialEndsAt, billingId, createdAt, updatedAt) plus nested agents[] and integrations[]. Returns `null` (HTTP 200, empty body) if the user has no org yet.

2) `POST /api/orgs` (controller line 40-51) → `orgsService.create({ name, slug, clerkUserId, email, userName })` (orgs.service.ts:55-104): if a User with that clerkId already exists it returns that user's existing Org (idempotent); otherwise creates Org (plan TRIAL, 3-day trialEndsAt) + nested OWNER User with `clerkId`, returning Org with `include: { users: true }`. Identity (clerkUserId) comes ONLY from the verified `sub`, never the body.

The same `clerkId == sub → orgId` mapping is enforced again on the org-scoped routes `GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/orgs/:id` and `:id/stats`, which additionally assert `id === @OrgId() orgId` (cross-org guard, controller lines 66/76/82/113) — i.e. you can only address your own resolved org id.
auth.bff_implication:
The BFF (artifacts/api-server) must STOP requiring an `org_id` JWT claim — its current middleware is BROKEN on this Clerk instance. In artifacts/api-server/src/middlewares/clerk-auth.ts:70-73, `requireClerkAuth` reads `payload['org_id']` and returns 403 "no org context in token" when absent. Because Clerk Organizations is disabled, `org_id` is NEVER present, so every authenticated request currently 403s.

REQUIRED CHANGES:
1. Verify the user JWT exactly as today (jose createRemoteJWKSet against CLERK_JWKS_URL, jwtVerify) — that part is correct and mirrors the backend. Keep `req.clerkUserId = payload.sub` and `req.clerkToken = token`.
2. Do NOT derive orgId from the token. Remove the `org_id` claim requirement / 403. The BFF has two valid options to obtain orgId:
   (a) PREFERRED — don't resolve orgId in the BFF at all for forwarding. apex-gtm-api's global OrgScopeGuard resolves org itself from the verified `sub` via the User table, so the BFF only needs to forward `Authorization: Bearer <user JWT>`. The upstream client (artifacts/api-server/src/upstream/apex-client.ts:40-41) already forwards the bearer token; the `x-org-id` header it also sends is IGNORED in prod (the guard only honors x-org-id when NODE_ENV!==production && ALLOW_DEV_ORG_HEADER===true) — harmless but unnecessary.
   (b) If the BFF itself needs orgId (e.g. for the OrgSettings response `orgId` field, caching, or its own logging), resolve it by calling upstream `GET /api/orgs/me` with the forwarded bearer token and read `org.id` from the returned Org (or `slug` etc.). It must NOT trust any client-supplied x-org-id and must NOT expect org_id in the JWT.

NET: on every call, (1) verify the user JWT (signature + exp), (2) forward `Authorization: Bearer <same JWT>` to apex-gtm-api and let the backend's OrgScopeGuard map sub→User.orgId; (3) if the BFF needs the concrete orgId for its own response/transform, fetch it once via `GET /api/orgs/me` and read `org.id`. The `x-org-id` header the BFF sends today is non-load-bearing in prod and can be dropped. Files: artifacts/api-server/src/middlewares/clerk-auth.ts (fix the 403 path), artifacts/api-server/src/upstream/apex-client.ts (token forward already correct).
